newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem says no sale of operations imminent.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem says no sale of operations imminent.

text.p: Despite industry rumors to the contrary, no sales of operating divisions at Bethlehem Steel Corp are imminent, company chairman Curtis "Hank" Barnette said on Wednesday.
Steel industry sources have speculated in recent weeks that the company's flat-rolled steel plant in Sparrows Point, Maryland, might either be on the auction block or a candidate for closure.
"We are not closing or selling Sparrows Point," Barnette told Reuters at the annual meeting of the American Iron and Steel Institute, the trade group that represents North American steel producers.
"We want that facility to be competitive," Barnette said. "It is a long-term part of this company."

Industry sources have speculated that Sparrows Point, which produces primarily hot-rolled sheet, a commodity product, would be sold or shut down by Bethlehem Steel because the plant was not as profitable as competing operations.
Barnette also said that the plant would possibly undergo a major modernization of its cold-rolling operations.

The plant's shipments are about three million tons per year. Bethlehem Steel and other major U.S. steelmakers in recent years have been shifting their product mix toward selling more cold-rolled and coated sheet steel, which fetch higher prices.
"Cold-rolling is a key part of this company," he said. "We are working on ways to make (Sparrows Point) more competitive."

Barnette said the company has begun a study involving the potential modernization of its Sparrows Point cold-rolling mill. That study has revealed that a new cold mill, which would supplement its existing mill, could be built either on site or outside the state of Maryland, he said.

"We could (build) an on-site brownfield mill that would be close to our current mill," he said. "Or, we could (build) it on site within 200 yards of the current mill on a greenfield site. The third alternative would be to build off site elsewhere in Maryland or in another appropriate state. All of these are market-driven decisions."
